topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, places the session within the broader cancer course, and outlines the main learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer as an Evolutionary Genetic Disease
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the fundamental biology of cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease driven by the cumulative acquisition of cellular mutations.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures and Epidemiological Evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the evidence that environmental exposures, rather than purely random biological bad luck, drive population-level cancer incidence.

topics.label: Infectious Agents and Oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how pathogens contribute to cancer development, using Burkitt lymphoma and its association with Epstein-Barr virus and malaria as a key example.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the molecular mechanisms through which chemical and physical carcinogens cause DNA damage and genetic mutations.

topics.label: Tumour Promotion, Microenvironment, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how non-mutagenic promotional processes and host tissue context provide the permissive conditions required for mutated cells to form tumours.

topics.label: Methodologies for Determining Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the scientific methodologies used to identify mutagenic exposures and evaluate whether environmental agents cause cancer.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk Assessment
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the lecturer's concluding remarks on the everyday balance between carcinogenic risks and practical benefits.
